perspective: Public-sector technical hiring manager conducting a two-minute application review, followed by inspection of lead-project and lab evidence.

reader_summary.target_role: Technical Project Manager focused on Product Operations, Implementation, civic technology, and public-facing technical systems.
reader_summary.central_value: Jamie turns ambiguous, stakeholder-heavy work into usable operating structure: requirements, workflows, decision records, documentation, launch support, onboarding, and durable handoffs.
proof_examples: Harry J. Epstein Company: maintained and improved e-commerce, analytics, marketing, content, and operational workflows, contributing to reported 2x revenue growth.
FairRentNYC / NYC Artist Coalition: co-founded the coalition and built public campaign websites plus 30+ pages of campaign-memory infrastructure, source maps, action tracking, and decision records.
CallNYC: built an independent prototype translating CouncilStat constituent-services data into resident-facing issue pathways and next-step guidance.
WOWList: co-built a community-calendar platform adopted across roughly 35 city ecosystems.
reader_summary.next_action: Invite Jamie to a first-round interview and use the linked resume and case studies to discuss implementation ownership, stakeholder coordination, and delivery methods.

evidence: The homepage immediately states “Technical Project Manager - Product Operations & Implementation.”

The first viewport says, “I create operating structure for complex public-facing teams” and explains the transformation from ambiguity into requirements, workflows, documentation, decision trails, launch support, onboarding, and handoffs.
The homepage supplies distinct, accurately bounded proofs for Harry J. Epstein Company, FairRentNYC, CallNYC, WOWList, and 196 / Sunday Dinner.
Visible actions include “View selected work,” “View resume,” “Contact Jamie,” and “Download resume PDF.”
findings: Role, value proposition, proof hierarchy, and application path are all legible within a two-minute review.
Collective and independent-project wording prevents mistaken claims of government employment, official authority, or solo policy causality.
scores.rationale: The application narrative is unusually explicit without requiring inference: I can identify the role family, repeat the central value in plain language, name more than three credible project proofs, and proceed directly to the resume or contact path.

evidence: The Harry J. Epstein page shows a captioned storefront screenshot with useful alt text, a July 2026 capture note, a public-site link, stated proof limits, source basis, and credits.

The FairRentNYC page shows a captioned campaign-site screenshot with useful alt text, a July 2026 capture note, collective-outcome language, a public-site link, source basis, and collaborator credits.

The CallNYC page shows a captioned archived prototype with useful alt text, an unofficial/non-current warning, links to the prototype, archived press, and public repository, plus explicit source limits.
The lab shows a captioned completion certificate and clearly limits it to professional development rather than proof of production SaaS or instructor affiliation.
Homepage and Technical Operations links lead to HJE, FairRentNYC, CallNYC, WOWList, and the lab.
findings: Each reviewed lead page has at least one genuine inspectable artifact.
Most additional gallery entries are descriptive cards rather than inspectable objects; the lab certificate proves evaluation coursework more directly than it proves the proposed team-memory method.
scores.rationale: The lead projects meet the application-ready threshold through genuine screenshots, captions, provenance, boundaries, and external destinations. The evidence set is not exceptional because several claimed operating artifacts are described rather than shown, and the lab’s strongest visual substantiates training rather than method performance.
scores.recommended_next_move: Add one public-safe, inspectable worked artifact to the Source-Backed Team Memory lab—such as a complete synthetic decision record with source links, review state, correction history, and final handoff—so the method itself carries the proof.

evidence: The Technical Operations page connects delivery coordination to HJE modernization, CallNYC’s resident-guidance prototype, and WOWList’s multi-city platform.
Risk surfacing and decision clarity connect to FairRentNYC campaign memory, its legislative source map and provenance redline, and KC Town Hall planning documentation.
Operating documentation connects to FairRentNYC’s 30+ pages, 196 / Sunday Dinner’s 300+ gatherings and 20+ resident artists, and the Source-Backed Team Memory method.
Public-facing launch and adoption connect to NYC Artist Coalition campaign websites, KC Spaces Fund infrastructure, CallNYC, WOWList, and HJE’s growth contribution.
Every named proof in these capability sections has a visible destination link.
findings: The page supports multiple hiring narratives: delivery coordination, risk and decision management, documentation and onboarding, and public launch/adoption.
Generic team-operations language is followed by specific project-action-result rows rather than being left as unsupported aspiration.
scores.rationale: The capability-to-proof mapping is exceptionally complete and easy to use in an application review. Named projects, Jamie’s actions or observable outcomes, and deeper links consistently reinforce the role-fit claims across more than three distinct narratives.

evidence: Lead case studies use a consistent early sequence: context, “What I did,” “What became usable,” and outcome/evidence.
The copy uses precise contribution language such as “helped,” “contributed,” “co-founded,” and “independent,” while preserving collective credit and scope limits.
CallNYC plainly states that it was not commissioned by the Council and is not an official or current service.
The homepage provides compact labels, project summaries, and direct application actions rather than presenting the portfolio as a raw claims registry.
findings: The voice is warm, precise, civic-minded, and trustworthy.
The homepage repeats the operating-structure/usable-systems thesis across the hero, capabilities, selected systems, operating motif, and “How I work.”
Case-study governance sections are credible but add substantial reading burden after the central proof is already established.
scores.rationale: The writing is strong and application-ready, with disciplined claims and clear project structure. It falls short of exceptional compression because the central thesis repeats and governance language occasionally competes with the hiring narrative.

overall_recommendation: Pass all four evaluated criteria. The candidate is application-ready and merits a first-round interview; the main remaining opportunity is stronger direct evidence of the lab method itself.
